evaluation: Leave-one-target-out over 5 SPHEREx fields (9-24 frames each), 10,000 test stamps per fold. Scores are from fold models; the shipped model is trained on all 5.
data: Trained and tested only on fake changes added to single real SPHEREx DR1/QR3 frames, never on two real dates. No real movers, no human labels.
selection: CNN chosen over trees on these same held-out folds and test stamps, so this is not an untouched benchmark.
limits: Labels change spots only; it does not find planets. Not tested on a real asteroid. Mover recall is 0.55 at S/N 3-5. A quarter of test stamps are movers; if real ones are rarer, more mover labels are wrong. The browser helper gives no label when the stamp is malformed; when the change is too faint, or over twice the brightest change in training; when image values exceed 131,072 noise units; when its channels disagree or nothing is localised; when the top two scores are close; or when a change more than 4 pixels from the centre is over 73 times the brightest change within 4 pixels of it. Otherwise the label covers the whole 15x15 stamp, so a brighter change away from the centre can decide it.
treesNote: Trees saw 600 stamps per class per target, the CNN 2,500: not like-for-like.
retest: Passed a frozen retest on fresh fake stamps (same fields and frames, not new sky): macro-F1 0.881, mover recall at S/N>=10 0.864, artifact precision 0.854. The last is a thin pass: its 95% range, 0.848-0.860, crosses the 0.85 target, and that range holds the 5 fields fixed, so it shows stamp-to-stamp noise only. Trees on the same fresh stamps: macro-F1 0.822.
weakField: WISE 0855 missed both 0.85 targets: mover recall at S/N>=10 0.725 (retest 0.741) and artifact precision 0.747 (retest 0.756); the trees did better on both. Barnard's Star has the lowest macro-F1 (0.848).
